rulings.restated: Divide helper "Business miles, as cents" by helper "Total miles, as cents", rounded to 6 decimal places; if the result is 1 or more, use 1 (and 0 if it is less than 0). Multiply column (d) by the result.
rulings.model: The IRS business/investment-use percentage for converted property must be figured only for the months used in business and multiplied by months/12; the restatement simply divides annual business miles by total miles without that conversion proration.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; the converted-vehicle months proration applies only to an owned vehicle converted from personal use in 2025, which scveh.screen refuses ("you converted it from personal use to business use during 2025"). Project stands.

rulings.restated: Divide helper "Business miles, as cents" by helper "Total miles, as cents", rounded to 6 decimal places; if the result is 1 or more, use 1 (and 0 if it is less than 0). Multiply column (d) by the result.
rulings.model: The IRS line is 'Depreciation and section 179 expense deduction'; the restatement instead computes Form 4562 Part V column (e), 'Basis for depreciation (business/investment use only),' by multiplying column (d) by business-use percentage, omitting the depreciation rate and passenger automobile limits.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; p946 pp. 61-62, Depreciation Worksheet for Passenger Automobiles, line 13, "Multiply line 12 by line 8. This is your business/investment cost". The handle 13 is that worksheet line, not Schedule C line 13; depreciation and the automobile limits are on later worksheet lines (scveh.macrs). Same point as the Claude ruling of this line. Project stands.

rulings.restated: Choose — [helper "Placed in service in 2025" = true → helper "Line 19 for a 2025 vehicle, half-year or mid-quarter"] [helper "Placed in service in 2025" = false → helper "Line 19 for a vehicle placed in service before 2025 (zero after the recovery period, when the worksheet is not used)"]
rulings.model: For a 2019 vehicle, the IRS says 'If the recovery period for an automobile ended before your tax year beginning in 2025, enter your unrecovered basis, if any, in column (h)' and permits deductions after the recovery period; the restatement returns zero for a 2019 vehicle.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; restatement accepted. Line 19 is a line of the automobile worksheet, which is not used after the recovery period; a 2019 vehicle's deduction is its unrecovered basis, limited and prorated (scveh.post, read by scveh.macrs_pass for column (h); Pub. 946 p. 61, Deductions After the Recovery Period), as stage14.veh.2019_cheap_mq3 asserts (BUG-0059).
